tasks.short: Prepare reports from synthesised test analyses

steps.what: Synthesize test analyses and establish report findings, recommendations and evidence references
Assemble technical reports using supplied findings, tables and source references
Check technical reports against analyses and approve the exact version for issue

tasks.design: Configure a report template in {DOCS} for already authored findings and referenced tables. The engineer performs synthesis and recommendations, then checks and approves the complete report before issue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring report sections and references were assembled manually after substantive analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and table links can repeat assembly without creating technical reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Determine what test results actually support and explain uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise conclusions that exceed the evidence.
tasks.altitude: Own the evidence chain from test to recommendation.

reach.learn: Keep identifiers, units and limitations attached to results

evidence.claim: Templates can assemble supplied findings and tables without replacing nuclear engineering analysis; savings are an unmeasured E1 task scenario.

assumptions: Existing test activities produce test results before s1. Their execution time is unchanged and earns no saving here.

In s1 the engineer performs synthesis and produces exact finding text, recommendation text, test identifiers, analysis versions, table references, units and limitations. Field capture, retrieval and clarification are included in its 45 hours.
No structured pass, safety or recommendation code is assumed ready. The template places text already written by the engineer.
Native templates are tried first; missing sources and unusual report structures revert to manual assembly and checking in s3.
unknowns: Repeatability of report sections and current templates
research_questions: Does template assembly save time after synthesis, field capture and final verification?

already_counted.description: Analysis synthesis, field capture and report approval

incremental.description: Template upkeep and source link reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact report version, findings, tables, references and recipient; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100, R=75 yields 25 gross and 17 net after 8 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-4 allows irregular reports and existing templates; substantive analysis remains full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare environmental impact material for agencies

steps.what: Establish environmental impact conclusions and assemble a referenced evidence pack for the agency audience
Draft reports or presentation wording from the checked evidence pack and authored conclusions

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory wording while preserving the engineer's conclusions
loop.input: Checked evidence pack, authored conclusions and section outline
loop.output: Draft wording with a source coverage map
loop.check: Engineer checks every factual assertion, limitation, numerical value and conclusion against the cited source passage
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; unsupported assertions or missing evidence return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use fixed sections and native templates first; only remaining explanatory prose needs language drafting

steps.what: Verify environmental statements and approve the final material before agency submission or presentation

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates for fixed sections and a bounded drafting step only for explanatory prose. The engineer supplies conclusions, checks every assertion and approves the exact report or presentation before it reaches the agency.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explanatory material must translate a large evidence set for a specific audience.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language drafting step can propose wording from an approved source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Determine impact significance and disclose uncertainties without understating them.
tasks.human_edge: Understand which limitations matter to the agency and affected people.
tasks.altitude: Own the completeness and defensibility of environmental communication.

reach.learn: Connect every public assertion to its supporting evidence

evidence.claim: Source bounded drafting may assist explanatory prose, but nuclear environmental reporting quality and labour effects remain E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the engineer selects current assessment versions, source passages, values with units, scope, required sections and exact conclusions. Evidence retrieval, structured capture, significance judgement and missing source resolution are counted in 45 hours.
No environmental acceptability or regulatory compliance flag is inferred by the drafting step.
s2's retained 24.5 hours include reading, checking and rewriting generated prose. s3 separately checks the assembled final material and performs issue approval.
Agency presentation time is retained in s3; any longer presentation remains human rather than being attributed to drafting savings.
Technical test reporting and environmental communication are separate outputs; shared evidence acquisition is assigned only once in a roll up.
unknowns: Share of material requiring new prose rather than fixed sections
research_questions: Does checked drafting reduce total preparation time without omitting environmental limitations?

already_counted.description: Evidence capture, prose verification and final issue review

incremental.description: Source pack maintenance and sampled output audit

approvals.approved_version: Exact environmental material, conclusions, limitations, references and recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100, R=89.5 gives 10.5 gross and 4.5 net after 6 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-2 allows heavy verification and limited reusable prose; impact assessment and presentation remain counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop remediation or restoration plans from site evidence, exposure pathways and practical constraints

tasks.design: Retain substantive remediation planning with the engineer using {DOCS}. Generic drafting does not replace selecting and justifying a site specific approach.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning depends on incomplete site evidence and long term consequences.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied evidence establishes replacement of the engineering judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Balance uncertain pathways, feasibility and consequences over time.
tasks.human_edge: Question whether the available evidence supports the proposed intervention.
tasks.altitude: Strengthen the transparency of remediation assumptions.

reach.learn: Connect engineering options to site uncertainties

evidence.claim: Site specific nuclear remediation planning remains engineering judgement; no task labour saving is established.

assumptions: The engineer evaluates evidence and develops the approach within s1; no ready made site risk or remediation suitability flag is assumed.
Existing investigations and simulation tools remain in their current workflows; no new administrative baseline is added.
No additional deployment or upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Site conditions, objectives and planning authority
research_questions: Which evidence gaps most constrain selecting a remediation approach?

incremental.description: No added operating system or service

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: substantive plan development remains fully human; zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design fuel cycle models to reduce waste

steps.what: Design fuel cycle models or processes and evaluate their implications for radioactive waste
outputs: fuel cycle model or process design

tasks.design: Keep model formulation and process design with the engineer, documented in {DOCS}. Existing numerical tools support the work but are not a new saving in this design task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful models require defensible assumptions and interpretation of technical trade offs.
tasks.enabler_now: No task specific automation improvement is established by the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Assess consequences beyond a nominal reduction in waste quantity.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an attractive numerical result rests on an unsuitable model.
tasks.altitude: Improve model validity and the clarity of design trade offs.

reach.learn: Distinguish model outputs from validated outcomes

evidence.claim: Fuel cycle model design remains engineering judgement; generic simulation capability does not establish a task labour saving.

assumptions: The engineer produces model assumptions, design choices and interpretation within s1, with no free validated design flag.
Existing calculations and simulations stay in the baseline; no unsupplied model or automatic process selection is proposed.
No new deployment or operating work means incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Model purpose, validation evidence and fuel cycle constraints
research_questions: Which assumptions most affect the apparent waste reduction?

already_counted.description: Model formulation, design and technical interpretation

incremental.description: No added software or monitoring process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: the design task remains fully counted, producing zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Own the evidence behind technical communication while preserving nuclear engineering judgement.
reach: Help environmental colleagues explain assessment and model limitations
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose reports are easier to assemble and audit while conclusions and designs remain professionally owned.
